    mesh-core, and the shell
    
    A window manager with no chrome has nowhere to put anything. Tiled mode
    was real, persisted per device and lockable by site policy, and until
    alt+t there was no way to turn it on -- not because it was unbuilt, but
    because nothing on the page could call it. Hotkeys fixed reachability and
    left discoverability: a control nobody can see is one only its author
    knows about.
    
    The chrome Extension is the smallest thing that makes the desktop
    legible: a bar with the open windows in it, a switch between windowed and
    tiled, and the host the windows mount into. It moves, resizes and stacks
    nothing -- those are the kernel's, because a broken chrome must not be
    able to make windows unresizable.
    
    Its first version registered its own handler table and every button did
    nothing. A description is data, so a function in it is referred to by id,
    and the id has to be one the renderer knows. Going through commands
    instead means the shell's actions are the same kind of thing as an
    Application's rather than a private arrangement -- nameable, rebindable,
    and reachable from anywhere a command is.
